rationale:
M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04), the `imports` type, and a KIND that was wrong rather than missing. The edge existed and the metadata was right; `type` read `references`. The measured cost: the one consumer that answers 'what does this module depend on' is the LSP usages file-level section, which filters on `relationship_type IN ('imports','exports')` (src/lsp/graph_request.ts, src/lsp/graph_usages.ts) — so a C++ include was invisible to it no matter what its metadata said. The C lane reached the same verdict for the identical construct and pins it there with c/macro-composed-include and the `c/include-kind-downgraded` mutant; `cpp/include-kind-downgraded` is this lane's counterpart, and BOTH the new kind and the absence of the old one are asserted here so a silent relabel cannot pass.

Four negative arms, and the second is the one that keeps this from being a label swap over everything:
  - a MACRO-COMPOSED include argument publishes no module and no edge of either kind (C-D2: the preprocessor is textual, so the path is not statically resolvable).
  - a `using` declaration at file scope is a NAMESPACE import, not file inclusion, and stays `references` + `using_dependency`. The two name different targets (`vector` vs `std::vector`) — so treating a using-directive as an include would make 'which headers does this file need' answerable with a using-declaration, which is a different question.
  - a class-body `using B::f;` is a member RE-EXPORT and publishes neither.
  - a function-local `using` is an execution artifact (the C lane's CGD20 rule, which this lane shares for typedefs).

The D3 arm is the EXACT COUNT, because it is the only assertion form that can fail on a duplicate: THREE `#include <vector>` directives produce THREE entries in the `imports` array ('how many times was it included' is a count the array keeps) and ONE `imports` edge ('what does this file depend on' is an edge). Both are asserted, so the count/edge split cannot be collapsed in either direction.

`fileLevel: true` and `module` are asserted because they are load-bearing rather than cosmetic: `parallel-indexer.ts` reads `metadata.fileLevel === true` to name the IMPORTING FILE on a row whose `source` is the file-scope sentinel `global`, which is the only way a `#include` edge can be attributed to a file in the store.

expectImports.comment: line 13. `<...>` makes it a system include; the name is the path node's text (M60/#924), never a slice of the whole directive.
line 14. A quoted include is not a system one.
line 15, the REPEAT. The array keeps every occurrence — the count — while the edge is deduplicated by D3.
line 27. `using namespace std;` — the namespace form carries the wildcard item.
line 28. `using std::pair;` carries the imported NAME, not the wildcard.

forbidImports.note: C-D2, literal-only: a macro-composed include argument is not a statically resolvable header name.
a class-body `using B::f;` is a member re-export, not a module dependency.
a function-local `using` is an execution artifact, not a declaration site — the CGD20 rule this lane shares for typedefs.

expectRelationships.note: M59.A7 (#825): the row's line is the PATH node's, not the directive's. `fileLevel` and `module` are what let the store attribute the edge to the importing FILE, because `source` is the file-scope sentinel.

THE TARGET IS NOW PINNED, BECAUSE IT IS NOW STABLE. It was left unconstrained while it was a PATH - a path varies with the checkout, and pinning one would have made the fixture a test of the machine. It is now the part's MODULE SYMBOL (its file stem), the same on every machine and the only form the arbiter can bind: MEASURED path => 0 resolved of 4,612 and symbol => 383 resolved of 4,612, same population, same 2,000-file stride sample, the target's FORM the only variable. A CONSTRAINT THAT CAN NOW BE PINNED IS A CHECK THAT SHOULD NOW BE OWNED, so this fixture asserts the stem itself rather than merely that some part_of row exists.

NEGATIVE ARM, the one that keeps this from being a label swap over everything: a `using` at file scope is a NAMESPACE import, so it stays `references`. Its target (`std`) is deliberately a DIFFERENT edge from the `#include <vector>` one (`vector`).

expectRelationshipCount.note: D3, as an EXACT count: THREE `#include <vector>` directives, THREE array entries, ONE edge. `expectRelationships` means '>= 1 match', so only `equals` can fail on a duplicate — which is how the first version of the D3 fixture passed against the pre-fix analyzer and the mutation harness had to say so.

D3 AS AN EXACT COUNT, ON THE PART KIND (R3, 2026-10-22): the quoted include is the unit's own fragment (src/ast/types.ts:148-160), so the dependency is ONE `part_of` edge with `metadata.partRole` = "part". `expectRelationships` means '>= 1 match', so only `equals` can fail on a duplicate — and the duplicate is exactly what a second push into the same `referencesSeen` key would produce. The TARGET is left unconstrained ON PURPOSE: a `part_of` target is a PATH built from the including file's directory, so it varies with the checkout, and pinning it would make this fixture a test of the machine. `equals: 1` is the fact (D3: one edge per dependency), and the PATH FORM is pinned on cpp/part-of-quoted-include. A CONSTRAINT THAT CAN NOW BE PINNED IS A CHECK THAT SHOULD NOW BE OWNED, so this fixture asserts the stem itself rather than merely that some part_of row exists.

forbidRelationships.note: THE DOWNGRADE ARM. A revert to `references` + metadata.isImport would leave every other assertion in this file passing and only this one failing, which is what makes it a regression gate for the relabel rather than a description of it.
the same downgrade on the quoted form.
a macro-composed argument must not fabricate an include edge of EITHER kind — mirrors c/macro-composed-include, which forbids both labels for this shape.

NEGATIVE ARM, asserted from the other direction: if a `using` were relabelled as `imports`, the two forbid rows and the two `references` rows above are what would catch it. One direction of a two-sided contract is not a contract.
the same, for the qualified using.
a class-body member re-export is not a module import.

C++20 `import` is ungrammatical on this parser (0 `import_declaration` nodes across 182 node types; the syntax ERROR-recovers into `declaration[type=import, declarator=std]`), so it must publish no import edge and the recovery artifact must not become a name.

A QUOTED include is not `imports` — it is `part_of` (src/ast/types.ts:148-160). The #910 concern is preserved, not retired: src/lsp/graph_request.ts and src/lsp/graph_usages.ts now read `part_of` as a FILE-LEVEL DEPENDENCY, so the row stays visible to the one surface that answers what a translation unit depends on.
